frontmatter.title: To sing a word the world refuses strikes the singer dumb.
The Order of the Measured Voice
The Tower is the loom of the Three Fates, the great frame on which the world was strung.
The Spinner, the Measurer and the Cutter wove the world.
Magic is the Fates' gift, lent to those who learn the proper rites.
The dead are in the Tower's walls.
The spirits are ancestors, demons or elementals.
The humming chamber beneath the shrine is holy ground, and no priest can say why.
The marks on the old plates are holy script.
What the Tower is stands written on the old plates, for those who collect the inscriptions and reconcile them.
The Tower is a machine, and magic is its by-product.
The seven points of the body have names on the old plates: Lumbar Anchor, Sacral Spool, Plexal Bellows, Sub-Clavicular Nodes, Glottal Reed, Pineal Resonator, Coronal Aperture.
The song is not only power but a lock, and to silence it is to open a door onto whatever the Tower was built over.
A rune is a sentence in the First Script, the language older than speech that holds the world together.
A glyph must be given room to breathe, or its voice arrives crowded.
Tight, sharp strokes carry heat and lightning; long, soft strokes carry weight and patience.
The quiet death: a word that argues with itself goes cold, and the Scribe feels the sting of it in the hand.
A rune that bursts and kills its maker was carved in anger: a word written with a hot heart turns on its writer.
Trace the glyph once in the air and count a slow breath along each line: if the breath comes ragged or runs out, the word will arrive crowded.
Spacing is checked with a measuring-cord; the Breath-Test is superstition.
Honest stone speaks truer than cut stone.
A master's true glyph is taught to no one and copied to no one.
The body is a river of Chi that runs in meridians and gathers at the seven Chakras; the points along the meridians are gates.

The three great Chakras are the Pineal at the brow, the Sub-Clavicular at the heart's gate and the Lumbar at the root of the spine; the lesser four sit at the crown, the throat, the navel and the seat.
In Mountain Stance the warrior widens and sinks until the mountain lends its weight.
To seal a gate is to close a door so the river finds another path.
A Chakra may be steeped in one of the five elements, wood, fire, earth, metal or water, the way a blade is tempered.
Within every gate the breath turns between yin and yang: strike from yang, recover in yin, and never loose a great blow from a gate at full ebb.
A strike must be given, not forced: the hand should arrive at the moment the breath crests, as the wave meets the shore.
A blow that dies in the hand was struck from an unclean gate, or anger was let into the Flow.
Master Vale of the Coiling Path turned his river inward with a devouring form, and it swallowed him whole.
The ancestral forms are finished: a thousand generations of masters have carried human potential to its summit.
Everything in the world has a true name, and to sing that name in its proper measure is to make the world remember what it is.
A chant is not only its notes but its measure: the rests are counted as carefully as the tones.
The Ground-Ohm, the Mendicant's Rest, is sung first in nearly every working.
Kharrian's Stride carries a working's power outward and makes a road for it across distance.
The Severing Sa releases a working all at once, and it is sung last.
The Unending Note fed upon itself and swallowed the choir that sang it.
The songbooks are complete: the old masters sang reality to its very limit.
A binder's first lesson is the ear, to hear the Listener's note under the world's noise; the second is the throat, to sing it back so truly that the spirit believes it has found kin.
The greater the god, the truer the note it demands.
Vareth the Long Cold is a frost-elemental of the high passes: her note is low and slow, her power vast and her pride immense.
Old Grandfather Ember is an ancestor-spirit of the forge-clans, warm and forgiving.
The Gull-Throat, Skerrin, is a fickle wind-spirit of the coast whose note will not hold still.
A pact is never taken; it is kept.
Honor its name, or it turns on you.
Halvarr the Bold sang to the Long Cold with a note that was almost true, and she turned on him.
To bind the greatest spirit is to hold the very ceiling of power.

The Summit & the Endings — Explaining Lore
The Summit & the Endings — In-World Lore
The Tower & the Weave — Explaining Lore
The Tower & the Weave — In-World Lore
The Tower is a machine: a hundred-register resonator raised over a puncture into the Chaos Matrix.
The Weave is an artifact of the Tower: magic can be worked because the Tower exists.
The Tower was built by a precursor civilization, the Tuners, who held the complete mathematics of the Weave.
Theos is the master resonance the Tower sustained: a song, not a god.
The Great Discord: the Tuners tried to make Theos self-sustaining, the cycle ran away and they were unwoven.
The spirits and the discordant masses are the unwoven Tuners: the dead builders.
The ~50% ceiling is lost know-how, not physics: every rune, form, chant and pact realises about half of what its structure could bear.
The Three Fates are a folk memory of the Tuners' operating triad: spool, measure and route, cut.
The ruins are the working parts of the dead machine, and the operator-plates carry the Tuners' notation, which is the real mathematics.
The Tower survived half-detuned; its broken song is why reality near it is soft and why volatility rises with height.
The apex gods are prior Conductors: climbers who took the seat and never left.
The dream is the disaster: a self-sustaining Theos is the runaway condition itself.
The Seal is false: nothing waits behind the silence, and the song can be ended safely.
Understanding can release the unwoven: in the Mending and the Silence the builders finish their unraveling and rest.
Deadening: opposed contributions cancel and the working goes silent; at root it is a mismatch of length or timing (E4).
Runaway: a working that feeds itself builds loop gain past the stability threshold and detonates as backlash (E6/E7).
A spirit is an external anchor with a fixed frequency; matching its song is the coherence lock, and the shiver is the mismatch beating toward zero (E5).
A proud spirit has high dominance, which narrows the tolerance of the lock: a truer match is required (E5).
A pact needs upkeep: the tone must be sustained at a continuous cost, and efficiency drops as it drifts (E9, E10).
A chant is a sequence of timed tones: pitch selects the element, and the spaces between syllables set the lengths from which phase is derived (E1, E2).
A rune is a hand-drawn specification of an oscillator graph: curvature is frequency, carving pressure is amplitude, and spacing becomes phase through propagation delay (E1, E2).
A rune fails by its geometry alone; the carver's mood plays no part.
Hand-carved, analog work tolerates wider mismatch than synthetic work (E5).
The body's meridian web is a graph that already exists, organised around seven chakra points; Chi is its oscillation, and a stance changes path lengths and so phase (E1, E2).
Each chakra point holds at most one elemental attunement, which deepens slowly and can be retrained only once it has fully faded, and a Yin-Yang polarity that is a dynamic balance.
